_comment: The shared fixtures for deployment-declaration.schema.json, so every reader of a deployment declaration runs the same ones. 'refusals' names, for each violation case of the two deployment rules in the corpus, the field the refusal is about and the values that field allows: a reader's test asserts its message names both, which is how 'rejected with the field and the allowed values' becomes checkable rather than a habit. A field is a path into deployment.json ('$' is the document), or, where 'in' is given, into that profile file. 'trees' are the cases the corpus cannot carry, because a wheel or a tarball carries no symbolic link and a corpus case is not a version-control work tree: each describes a tree that a reader's own test builds on disk - writing 'files', creating each of 'links' as a symbolic link to its relative target, and making the tree root a work tree when 'workTree' is set - and then runs the rule over 'projectRoot'. 'resolve' lists the paths the declaration leads a reader to, each relative to its 'base', and where each lands against the checkout: the root of the work tree that holds the project, or the project root itself when it lies in none. Every name, host and image here is invented.

violation-02.allowed: one JSON object, not an array

violation-03.allowed: a unit's keys: backup, command, dependsOn, env, healthPath, id, instances, kind, livenessPath, migrations, role, size, stateful, version - there is no image key: name a datastore by kind and version, or build the unit from the checkout

violation-04.allowed: a unit's keys, among them stateful

violation-05.allowed: the top-level keys: build, compose, externalDatabase, rollback, schemaVersion, sizes, units, volumes - an environment is the deploying tool's record, not this file

violation-09.allowed: beside unmanaged, only reason and schemaVersion

violation-10.allowed: a sentence saying why a tool cannot drive this deploy

violation-11.allowed: a sentence that is not blank

violation-13.allowed: an argument list of strings, never a shell string

violation-19.allowed: a policy with every and keep - client is valid only on externalDatabase

violation-20.allowed: an ISO 8601 duration, such as P1D or PT6H

violation-22.allowed: the datastore version, declared with its kind: 17 for postgres

violation-23.allowed: a version the datastore table carries for postgres: 17

violation-24.allowed: an id no other unit has

violation-25.allowed: a path relative to the project root, with forward slashes

violation-26.allowed: a path that resolves inside the checkout

violation-27.allowed: a deployment profile, never the development one (docker-compose.yml)

violation-28.allowed: a deployment profile, never the development one the development declaration names (compose.dev.yml)

violation-29.allowed: true - a backup policy sits only on a unit declared stateful

violation-30.allowed: nothing - approvals is deploy policy: it belongs to the deploying tool's environment policy, not to this file

violation-31.allowed: nothing - publishers is deploy policy: it belongs to the deploying tool's environment policy, not to this file

violation-32.allowed: nothing - access is deploy policy: it belongs to the deploying tool's environment policy, not to this file

violation-33.allowed: nothing - gatePolicy is deploy policy: it belongs to the deploying tool's environment policy, not to this file

violation-34.allowed: nothing - requiredApprovals is deploy policy: it belongs to the deploying tool's environment policy, not to this file

violation-35.allowed: a build context that resolves inside the checkout

violation-38.allowed: an upper-case variable name, as the variable manifest declares one

violation-40.allowed: true, or leave the key out

violation-01.allowed: a service of the profile: api, db, migrate, web

violation-02.allowed: a profile file that exists, whose services the units are

violation-03.allowed: a named volume of the profile: db-data

violation-04.allowed: a name the profile passes to api

violation-05.allowed: a name routed to a file api loads - the manifest routes this one to .app.worker.env

violation-06.allowed: the profile's command for worker: terp jobs worker

violation-07.allowed: the profile's start order for api, restricted to declared units: db, migrate

violation-08.allowed: a profile image that is the datastore table's digest for postgres 17

violation-09.allowed: a profile image that is the datastore table's digest for postgres 17, from the table's own registry

violation-10.allowed: a profile image that is the datastore table's digest for postgres 17

violation-11.allowed: an image some profile service builds from the checkout

violation-12.allowed: a resolved profile that runs no database service

violation-13.allowed: a resolved profile that runs no database service

violation-14.allowed: a role that resolves it: api, database, one-shot, scheduler, store, web or worker

violation-15.allowed: the resolved profile's command for worker: terp jobs worker --once
